audit_findings.title: One-time property gains may inflate the FY2026 anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $11.5m pretax; $8.5m using the filed 25.9% FY2026 effective tax rate, equal to 8.7% of the $97.7m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Nonrecurring gains enter anchor owner earnings and are capitalized through the operating DCF, while subsequent lease expense remains recurring.
audit_findings.evidence: Partially offsetting the items above, SG&A expense as percentage of sales in fiscal 2026 decreased due to a $7.6 million and $3.9 million gain on the sale of buildings and fixed assets related to sale-leaseback transactions of four retail stores and our Casegoods headquarters building, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The gains are demonstrated, but their omission from the owner-earnings adjustment ledger is unresolved. If both remain, the base operating value is overstated by approximately $113m, or $2.66 per share, using the model's base operating-PV-to-anchor ratio. That is large relative to the $4.19 difference between base value and market price and could reverse the bear-case conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace both gains through the FY2026 owner-earnings ledger, verify their after-tax removal without reversing continuing rent, and rerun all scenarios if either remains.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may omit the reinvestment required to produce it
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2027 capex guidance of $90m-$110m is $13.7m-$33.7m above FY2026 capex of $76.3m, equivalent to 14.0%-34.5% of the $97.7m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Required maintenance or sustaining capital reduces owner earnings; expansion capital must also be funded when the forecast credits the resulting growth.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect capital expenditures to be in the range of $90 to $110 million for fiscal 2027, with continued spending on our distribution and home delivery transformation, manufacturing-related investments, and investments in our La-Z-Boy store (new stores and remodels).
audit_findings.explanation: The higher spending program is demonstrated, but its maintenance, transformation, and discretionary-growth components are not separated. Even the bottom-of-range increase is large relative to anchor owner earnings, so omission of a recurring or growth-required portion is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the capex project schedule, classify each project as maintenance, margin-preserving transformation, or discretionary expansion, link expansion spending to scenario growth, and rerun owner earnings and growth scenarios with the required cash outlays.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition-funded growth may be credited without its cash cost
audit_findings.magnitude: $86.4m of acquisition cash in FY2026 and $15.7m in Q1 FY2027, equal to 88.4% and 16.1% of the $97.7m anchor, respectively
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquisition and store-opening cash costs sit outside ordinary capex and owner earnings but may be necessary to achieve forecast growth.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to grow our Retail segment through organic same-store sales growth and by increasing company-owned stores through the opening of new stores and acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: The acquisition strategy and substantial cash spending are demonstrated; whether the modeled 2%-4% growth includes acquisition-driven growth without funding is unresolved. FY2026 same-store written sales declined 3%, while reported growth benefited from acquisitions and new stores, making the potential mismatch material.
audit_findings.action: Decompose each scenario into organic same-store growth, new-store growth, and acquired-store growth; identify purchase prices, opening costs, integration spending, and working capital for the latter two; then rerun or exclude unfunded growth.

audit_findings.title: Committed fiscal 2027 restructuring costs may be missing
audit_findings.magnitude: $17.3m of Q1 FY2027 pretax charges: $9.3m impairment, $3.0m primarily severance, and $5.0m mixed severance, accelerated depreciation, and lease expense; cash portion and remaining costs unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Genuine closure, severance, transfer, lease, and duplicate-running cash outflows reduce near-term forecast owner earnings but should not necessarily reduce normalized terminal earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: The financial impact of these actions will primarily be recognized during fiscal 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: The charges are now demonstrated in the latest 10-Q, but the record does not show their cash portion, additional costs through the end of FY2027, or their treatment in the forecast. The recorded $17.3m equals 1.1% of base equity value and at most $0.41 per share if treated entirely as undiscounted cash, but unquantified remaining transfer and duplicate-running costs prevent a complete materiality conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the Q1 charges by cash versus noncash component, obtain expected remaining FY2027 closure and transfer cash flows, trace them into forecast years, and rerun the DCF using only genuine cash outflows.

audit_findings.title: A warranty-liability release may be embedded in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.606m pretax liability release; $4.15m using the filed 25.9% FY2026 effective tax rate, equal to 4.3% of the $97.7m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The nonrecurring liability release increases reported earnings, while recurring upfront dealer service allowances remain an operating expense.
audit_findings.evidence: SG&A expense as a percentage of sales decreased 50 basis points in fiscal 2026, compared with the prior year, from lower warranty expense due to a reduction in our warranty liability driven by a change in which we provide external dealers an upfront service allowance for certain labor and delivery costs for La-Z-Boy products that they sell and have previously sold.
audit_findings.explanation: The $5.606m release is demonstrated, but its removal from the owner-earnings ledger is unresolved. If embedded after tax, it would overstate base value by approximately $55m, or $1.30 per share, using the model's base operating-PV-to-anchor ratio; that is sufficient to reverse the narrow bear-case premium to market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace the warranty-policy change through net income, operating cash flow, working-capital adjustments, and the owner-earnings ledger; confirm the release is removed once and recurring service allowances remain; then rerun all scenarios if necessary.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may treat non-excess foreign cash as distributable
audit_findings.magnitude: $62.3m of foreign cash at April 25, 2026, equal to 22.8% of the $272.66m bridge and $1.47 per diluted share; other operating-cash and repatriation constraints unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Only excess, distributable cash belongs in the equity bridge; trapped, tax-frictioned, customer-supported, or minimum operating cash requires exclusion or a haircut.
audit_findings.evidence: Included in our cash and cash equivalents at April 25, 2026, was $62.3 million held by foreign subsidiaries, the majority of which we have determined to be permanently reinvested.
audit_findings.explanation: The model demonstrably adds the entire July cash and short-term-investment balance, while the filing demonstrates that most of the earlier $62.3m foreign balance was permanently reinvested. The July jurisdictional balance and actual surplus requirement remain unresolved. The disclosed foreign balance alone exceeds the approximately $41.7m equity premium of the bear value over market price, so plausible bridge adjustments can change that conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the July 25 cash balance by entity and jurisdiction, quantify repatriation taxes and restrictions, establish minimum operating cash using working-capital and customer-deposit requirements, and rerun the bridge with only demonstrably excess cash.
